subject: Commerce
title: International Trade
outline: Meaning, types and basis of international trade
Differences between home and foreign trade
Balance of trade and balance of payments
Terms of trade and exchange rates
Trade barriers, protection and economic groupings

modules.title: Nature and Basis of International Trade
modules.html:
Meaning

International (foreign/external) trade is the exchange of goods and services across national boundaries. Its branches are import trade, export trade and entrepot (re-export) trade.

Basis

  1. Uneven distribution of natural resources
  2. Differences in climate, soil and technology
  3. Specialisation and comparative cost advantage
  4. Differences in the cost and skill of labour
  5. Desire for variety and larger markets

Home Trade vs Foreign Trade

BasisHome tradeForeign trade
BoundaryWithin one countryAcross countries
CurrencyOne currencyDifferent currencies; exchange rate needed
DocumentsFew and simpleMany – bill of lading, certificate of origin, etc.
BarriersFewTariffs, quotas, embargoes
TransportMainly road/railMainly sea and air
RiskLowerHigher (marine, political, exchange)

Protection of Trade

Instruments: tariffs (import duties), quotas, embargoes, exchange control, subsidies to local firms, administrative bottlenecks. Reasons: infant industry argument, employment protection, revenue, retaliation, correcting adverse balance of payments, national security. Dangers: retaliation, inefficiency, higher prices and smuggling.

Economic Groupings

ECOWAS, AfCFTA, AU, OPEC, EU, WTO and IMF/World Bank shape modern trade rules and finance.

examples.q: Nigeria exports crude oil worth $48bn and imports goods worth $56bn in a year. Determine the balance of trade and comment.
examples.a: \( \text{Balance of Trade} = 48 - 56 = -\$8\text{bn} \) – an unfavourable (adverse/deficit) balance of trade because visible imports exceed visible exports. It may be offset by invisible earnings or capital inflows.

examples.q: Explain the infant industry argument for protection and one danger of applying it too long.
examples.a: New domestic industries cannot yet compete with established foreign firms; temporary tariffs let them grow to an efficient scale. If protection lasts too long the industry becomes complacent and permanently inefficient, and consumers pay high prices indefinitely.

modules.title: Balance of Payments and Exchange Rate
modules.html:
Balance of Trade (BOT)

The difference between the value of visible exports and visible imports.

$$\text{BOT} = \text{Visible Exports} - \text{Visible Imports}$$

Balance of Payments (BOP)

A systematic record of ALL economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world in a year. Components:

  1. Current account – visible trade + invisible trade (services, income, transfers).
  2. Capital and financial account – long- and short-term capital flows, direct and portfolio investment.
  3. Official settlements/monetary movements – changes in external reserves.

Causes of BOP Deficit

  • Heavy dependence on imports and on a single export commodity
  • Fall in world prices of exports
  • Inflation making exports uncompetitive
  • Debt servicing and profit repatriation
  • Capital flight

Correcting a Deficit

  1. Devaluation of the currency
  2. Import restrictions (tariffs, quotas)
  3. Export promotion and diversification
  4. Deflationary fiscal and monetary policy
  5. Exchange control and foreign borrowing (short-term relief)

Terms of Trade

$$\text{Terms of Trade} = \dfrac{\text{Index of Export Prices}}{\text{Index of Import Prices}} \times 100$$

A figure above 100 means favourable terms of trade.

Exchange Rate

The price of one currency in terms of another. Devaluation is a deliberate official reduction in the value of a currency under a fixed system; depreciation is a market-driven fall under a floating system.

examples.q: Export price index is 138 and import price index 120. Calculate the terms of trade and interpret.
examples.a: \( \text{TOT} = \dfrac{138}{120}\times100 = 115 \). Since 115 > 100, the terms of trade are favourable: a given volume of exports now buys more imports than in the base year.

examples.q: Given visible exports ₦25tn, visible imports ₦28tn, invisible receipts ₦9tn and invisible payments ₦4tn, find the current account balance.
examples.a: Visible balance \(=25-28=-₦3\text{tn}\). Invisible balance \(=9-4=+₦5\text{tn}\). Current account \(=-3+5=+₦2\text{tn}\), a surplus, showing that services and transfers more than offset the trade gap.

modules.title: Documents and Procedure in Foreign Trade
modules.html:
Key Documents

DocumentPurpose
IndentOrder from a foreign buyer, often through an agent
Bill of ladingReceipt for goods shipped, evidence of contract of carriage and document of title
Airway bill / consignment noteEquivalent for air/land carriage (not a document of title)
Certificate of originStates the country where goods were produced; used for tariff purposes
Marine insurance policy/certificateCovers the goods against sea perils
Commercial invoiceFull details of goods, prices and terms
Consular invoiceInvoice certified by the importer's consul to prevent dumping/under-invoicing
Bill of exchangeUnconditional written order to pay; used to finance the trade
Letter of creditBank guarantee of payment to the exporter
Form M / Form NXPNigerian import and export documentation for forex and customs
Ship's manifestList of all cargo on board
Bill of sight / entryCustoms documents for goods of uncertain description / clearing

Delivery Terms

  • FOB (Free on Board) – seller pays until goods are loaded on ship.
  • CIF (Cost, Insurance and Freight) – price includes insurance and freight to destination port.
  • Ex-works – buyer collects at the factory gate.
  • Franco – seller bears all costs to the buyer's premises.

Bonded Warehouse

A warehouse under customs supervision where dutiable imports are stored until duty is paid, allowing the importer to defer payment or re-export duty-free.

examples.q: An importer buys goods FOB Rotterdam at €40,000; freight is €2,500 and marine insurance €800. If €1 = ₦1,750, compute the CIF value in naira.
examples.a: CIF (€) \(=40{,}000+2{,}500+800=€43{,}300\). In naira \(=43{,}300\times1{,}750=₦75{,}775{,}000\). Import duty would then be assessed on this CIF value plus any port charges.

examples.q: Why is a bill of lading described as a document of title while an airway bill is not?
examples.a: A bill of lading can be endorsed and transferred, so possession of the original entitles the holder to claim the goods – it represents ownership in transit. An airway bill is merely a receipt and contract of carriage; the named consignee alone can take delivery, so it cannot be negotiated.

quiz.q: International trade differs from home trade mainly because of
quiz.solution: Foreign trade involves currency conversion, customs barriers and more documents.
Goods are imported and then re-exported, often after minor processing.

quiz.q: The balance of trade considers only
quiz.solution: BOT compares visible exports and visible imports of goods.

options: All economic transactions with other countries
quiz.solution: BOP covers current, capital/financial and official settlement accounts.

quiz.q: Which is an invisible export for Nigeria?
quiz.solution: Services such as shipping, tourism and banking earnings are invisible trade.

quiz.q: A deliberate official reduction in the value of a currency is
quiz.solution: Devaluation is an official act under a fixed exchange-rate regime.

quiz.q: Terms of trade are favourable when the index is
quiz.solution: An index above 100 means export prices rose faster than import prices.

quiz.q: The document of title to goods sent by sea is the
quiz.solution: It is negotiable and transfers ownership of goods in transit.

quiz.q: A consular invoice is used mainly to
quiz.solution: It is certified by the consul to confirm true value and description.
The quoted price covers cost of goods plus insurance and freight.

options: Under customs supervision until duty is paid
quiz.solution: It allows deferment of duty and duty-free re-export.

quiz.q: A quota is a restriction on
quiz.solution: Quotas physically limit the volume that may be imported.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a way of correcting a BOP deficit?
An adverse balance of trade occurs when
quiz.solution: More is spent on visible imports than earned from visible exports.
New industries need shelter until they attain competitive scale.

quiz.q: Which organisation regulates world trade rules?
quiz.solution: The World Trade Organisation supervises trade agreements and settles disputes.
